 Petrol, Diesel Prices Today, November 11, 2026: Check Latest Rates in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad
 Authored By HDFC SKY | Published at: Nov 11, 2026 09:41 AM IST

 Mumbai, November 11 : Petrol and diesel prices today, November 11, remained unchanged across major Indian cities, including Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai and Bengaluru. Petrol was priced at Rs 102.12 per litre in Delhi and Rs 111.21 in Mumbai, while diesel rates stood at Rs 95.20 and Rs 97.83 per litre, respectively.    
 Crude oil prices rebounded on Wednesday, November 11, after falling to two-month lows in the previous session, as fresh attacks on shipping vessels in the Strait of Hormuz revived concerns over global energy supplies. The recovery came as investors weighed hopes of de-escalation in the Iran war against persistent security risks along one of the world’s most critical oil transit routes.   
 Brent crude futures rose 1.14% to $92.5 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 0.7% to $86.7 per barrel. Both benchmarks had declined sharply in the previous session, with prices initially falling more than $3 a barrel after US officials played down the possibility of further military strikes against Iran.   
 Fresh attacks on commercial vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz have complicated expectations of a sustained recovery in global oil supplies. According to the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, 37 ships were attacked in the strait and surrounding waterways in October, the highest monthly tally since the beginning of the war. Another 10 attacks have been reported so far in November.   
 Videos verified by Reuters showed a tanker on fire near the coast of Oman on Sunday, while another vessel was struck northeast of Oman’s Lima on Tuesday, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards Navy also said two tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines while using what it described as an unauthorised route through the strait.   
 The continuing attacks have raised doubts about how quickly shipping activity can normalise, even if a diplomatic agreement is reached. Analysts at LSEG noted that restoring traffic would require mine clearance, lower insurance costs and a willingness among shipowners to resume voyages through the waterway.   
 Oil markets have also been responding to conflicting signals surrounding diplomatic efforts to end the Iran conflict. Prices initially declined on Tuesday after US officials suggested there was little need for further military action, but recovered some losses after an Iranian security official said no negotiations were taking place between the two sides.   
 Meanwhile, US crude inventories rose by 9 million barrels in the week ended November 6, according to data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), adding to concerns over near-term supply availability.   
 In another development, Russian oil refining capacity has declined by around 30% since late October following renewed Ukrainian drone attacks, according to industry sources. Russian and Ukrainian officials also held their first peace talks since February in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, as US President Donald Trump’s envoys renewed efforts to end the conflict.   
 For oil markets, the balance between geopolitical supply disruptions, the prospect of diplomatic progress and inventory trends is likely to remain a key determinant of price movements in the near term.   
 Check the latest city-wise petrol and diesel prices across India, including Gurgaon, Noida, Hyderabad, Jaipur and Lucknow.   
 Petrol Prices   
 Petrol prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities and state capitals on Wednesday, November 11, with oil marketing companies keeping retail rates steady. In New Delhi, petrol was priced at Rs 102.12 per litre, while Mumbai continued to have one of the highest rates among the four metropolitan cities at Rs 111.21 per litre.   
 Among other metros, petrol was retailing at Rs 113.51 per litre in Kolkata and Rs 107.76 per litre in Chennai. In Bengaluru, the fuel was priced at Rs 111.68 per litre, while Hyderabad recorded a higher rate of Rs 116.15 per litre.   
 In the National Capital Region (NCR), petrol was selling at Rs 102.97 per litre in Gurgaon and Rs 101.96 per litre in Noida. Chandigarh recorded a rate of Rs 101.54 per litre, while Lucknow had petrol prices at Rs 101.89 per litre. Jaipur and Patna reported rates of Rs 113.19 and Rs 113.37 per litre, respectively.   
 Among other state capitals, petrol was priced at Rs 108.97 per litre in Bhubaneswar and Rs 115.49 per litre in Thiruvananthapuram. There was no change in petrol prices across any of the listed cities compared with the previous day’s rates.   
 Diesel Prices   
 Diesel prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities and state capitals on Wednesday, November 11, with oil marketing companies keeping retail rates steady. In New Delhi, diesel was priced at Rs 95.20 per litre, while Mumbai recorded a rate of Rs 97.83 per litre.   
 Among the other metropolitan cities, diesel was selling at Rs 99.82 per litre in Kolkata and Rs 99.55 per litre in Chennai. In Bengaluru, the fuel was priced at Rs 99.56 per litre, while Hyderabad recorded a significantly higher rate of Rs 104.23 per litre.   
 In the National Capital Region (NCR), diesel was retailing at Rs 95.64 per litre in Gurgaon and Rs 95.44 per litre in Noida. Chandigarh had one of the lowest rates at Rs 89.47 per litre, while Lucknow recorded a price of Rs 95.36 per litre. Diesel was priced at Rs 98.25 per litre in Jaipur and Rs 99.36 per litre in Patna.   
 Among other state capitals, diesel was selling at Rs 100.68 per litre in Bhubaneswar and Rs 104.40 per litre in Thiruvananthapuram, the highest among the listed cities. There was no change in diesel prices across any of the cities compared with the previous day’s rates.
